# =============================================================================
# tessera-term: device reports and the PTY reply path (DA, DSR, XTVERSION, DECRQM, DECRQSS, XTWINOPS)   (issue #10 part 1, wave 8)
# crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/reports_spec.txt   (spec-researcher output, 2026-10-31)
# Companion: reports_spec.notes.md (identity, level 5, unknown cell size, xterm-vs-spec table, "Done when" amendments).
#
# FORMAT (one table-driven test, tests/reports.rs, through common::check_table; every failing id is reported)
#   ### ID               unique row id; the prefix names the group (DA, DSR, XV, RM, RQ, WO, TS, KT, RP).
#   size: RxC            grid size (default for an omitted size would be 24x80; every row states it).
#   step: feed <bytes>   \e \x1b \\ \r \n \xNN \u{H} escapes as in the other fixtures. The test also runs each row once
#                        with the bytes split at EVERY offset (Chunking) and the replies must be identical.
#   step: set cell_px <W>x<H>   Terminal::set_cell_pixels(width, height) (pixels per cell). Rows without it have the
#                        cell size UNKNOWN (never set), which is the state before the first frame.
#   step: set title <text>      the title the terminal last emitted (same as feeding OSC 2 ; text ST; shorthand).
#   reply: <bytes>|none  EXACT bytes the terminal queued as Request::Reply since the previous `reply:` line (or the start),
#                        concatenated in order. `none` = no Reply request at all. Replies are ALWAYS 7-bit (ESC [ , ESC P,
#                        ESC \ ), also after DECSCL Pc=0/2 (S8C1T is #96's job, wave 9). `<VERSION>` stands for
#                        env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") of the tessera-term crate.
#   requests: [..]       OPTIONAL: non-Reply requests drained after the steps above it: `SetTitle("..")` and `Resize(r,c)`;
#                        omitted = not asserted. Reply requests are never listed here.
#   screen:/cursor:      OPTIONAL, as csi_spec.txt (`>` rows, `|` after the cursor cell), only where "the query must not print
#                        or swallow text" is the point.
#   cite:                the spec/source for the row. note: free text. flags: decision (D-xxx below) | xterm-quirk |
#                        negative | unverified | security | control
#
# PRIMARY SOURCES (fetched 2026-10-31)
#   [CTL]  xterm ctlseqs https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.txt (patch 412 snapshot; section names as in the text)
#   [XT]   xterm source, ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots master, as fetched 2026-10-31 (version.h XTERM_PATCH 412):
#            charproc.c L4098..4186 CASE_DA1; L4224..4283 CASE_DA2; L4284..4300 CASE_DECRPTUI (DA3); L4599..4746 CASE_DSR/CPR;
#            L5462..5471 CASE_REPORT_VERSION (XTVERSION); L5087..5130 CASE_DECSCL; L8979.. window_ops; L9142..9235 14/16/18/19 t;
#            L9260..9320 22/23 t; misc.c L5388..5470 do_ansi_rqm; L5470..5890 do_dec_rqm; L4880..5030 DECRQSS (do_dcs);
#            misc.c L3252..3316 xtermFormatSGR; misc.c L7976..8030 xtermPushTitle/xtermPopTitle; ptyx.h L2371 MAX_SAVED_TITLES 10;
#            version.c xtermVersion() -> "XTerm(412)"; xterm.man disallowedWindowOps default
#            "GetChecksum,GetIconTitle,GetSelection,GetWinTitle,SetSelection,SetXprop" (so 14/16/18/19/22/23 t are ALLOWED by default).
#   [DEC]  DEC STD 070 / VT510 RM https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/ (DA, DSR, DECRQM, DECRPM, DECRQSS, DECSCL chapters); VT520 RM for level 5.
#   [VT]   tmux tty-keys.c (master): reads DA1 params 4, 21, 28, 52 only when the first param is 61..65; DA2 first param 77/84/85 =
#          mintty/tmux/urxvt; XTVERSION name prefixes "XTerm(", "iTerm2 ", "mintty ", "foot(", "kitty(", "WezTerm "; DECRPM ?2026.
#          vim term.c (master): t_RV=ESC[>c, t_u7=ESC[6n, t_RC=ESC[?12$p, t_RS=ESC P$q q ST, t_ST/t_RT=ESC[22;2t / ESC[23;2t,
#          t_Si/t_Ri=ESC[22;1t / ESC[23;1t, t_KS-query ESC[?u; handle_version_response: DA2 Pv >= 95 mouse drag, >= 277 SGR mouse,
#          Pp=1 with Pv 4000..4009 = kitty, >= 2500 = "not xterm" (no xterm-specific quirks, still SGR mouse).
#          neovim tui.c (master): ESC[?u ESC[c (kitty probe then DA1 as sentinel), ESC[0m ESC[4:3m ESC P$qm ST (curly underline
#          probe), ESC]11;? BEL ESC[5n (bg colour then DSR 5 as sentinel), DECRQM ?69 ?2026 ?2027 ?2031 ?2048, final ESC[c at exit,
#          ESC[22;0t / ESC[23;0t title stack.
#   [KT]   kitty docs https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/ (keyboard protocol "Detection of support": CSI ? u then CSI c; DECRQSS m returns 4:3).
#   [CS]   Contour synchronized-output spec https://gist.github.com/christianparpart/d8a62cc1ab659194337d73e33e3ae6ed (DECRQM ?2026
#          answers 1 or 2 when supported, 0 when not).
#   Not verified here (no network access to the product): iTerm2, WezTerm and Alacritty reply strings are quoted from memory only where a
#   row says "(from memory)"; xterm rows are read from the source above.
#
# DECISIONS (D-xxx; the lead confirms, the rows follow the recommendation):
#   D-ID      Tessera is NOT xterm-compatible by identity. XTVERSION = DCS > | Tessera <VERSION> ST (space, no parenthesis, so no
#             tmux name prefix matches and tmux falls back to terminfo + DA1). DA2 = CSI > 1 ; <PV> ; 0 c with Pp=1 (VT220-class, as
#             kitty, foot and Ghostty answer); Pc is always 0. Never Pp 77/84/85 (tmux reads them as mintty/tmux/urxvt) nor Pp=1 with
#             Pv 4000..4009 (vim reads that as kitty).
#   D-DA2PV   NEEDS THE LEAD (rows use the placeholder <PV> = the test's constant reports::DA2_PV, so the value can change without
#             touching rows). vim term.c handle_version_response reads Pv: < 95 no mouse-drag reporting, 95..276 X10-style drag only,
#             >= 277 SGR mouse, >= 2500 "not an xterm" (skips xterm-only quirks, still SGR-capable). Recommendation: Pv >= 2500, encoded
#             `10000 + minor*100 + patch` (0.1.0 -> 10100; stays below vim's 20000 "rxvt" cut). Alternative: `major*10000+minor*100+patch`
#             (0.1.0 -> 100), which is how Alacritty/foot encode it but would leave vim without SGR mouse.
#   D-DA1     DA1 first parameter is 60 + conformance_level() (DECSCL changes it, as on the VT510/VT520; xterm itself keeps the
#             decTerminalID resource and ignores DECSCL here, xterm-quirk). Level 1 (VT100) answers CSI ? 1 ; 2 c (xterm's VT100 form).
#             Levels 2..5 answer CSI ? 6<L> ; 22 c : only features Tessera implements (22 = ANSI colour). NOT advertised: 1 (132
#             columns: DECCOLM never resizes), 2 (printer), 3, 4 (no ReGIS/Sixel), 6 (selective erase, #95), 8, 9 (NRCS, #112), 15,
#             16, 17, 18, 21 (#97), 28 (rectangular editing), 29, 52 (clipboard: OSC 52 is write-only, tmux would then try to read).
#             Feature numbers are added when the issue that implements them lands.
#   D-L5      Level 5 (reachable through CSI 65 " p, #92; xterm with id 420 rejects 65) answers as a VT525 (DEC STD 070 / xterm
#             decTerminalID=525): DA1 CSI ? 65 ; 22 c, DECRQSS " p -> 65 ; 1 " p. Alternative (clamp to 4) rejected: the level is
#             stored, so the reply must follow it. DA2 does NOT follow the level (xterm: it follows the resource, not DECSCL).
#   D-DA3     CSI = c answers DCS ! | 00000000 ST (xterm DECRPTUI: site code and serial zero) at level >= 4, silence below (xterm).
#   D-DECID   ESC Z (DECID) answers exactly like DA1 (xterm CASE_DECID -> DA1 reply).
#   D-DSRSET  DEC DSRs answered: ?6 (DECXCPR), ?15, ?25, ?26, ?55, ?56, ?75, ?85 with xterm's level gates; ?53, ?62, ?63 and every
#             other Ps stay silent (a documented subset; the brief allows it).
#   D-CELLPX  Unknown cell size: CSI 14 t / CSI 16 t stay SILENT (no zero reply: a zero cell size divides by zero in clients).
#             Once set_cell_pixels(w,h) was called with w,h > 0 they answer. 18 t and 19 t never need pixels.
#   D-WIN2    CSI 14;2 t (whole-window pixels) is silent: Tessera's terminal does not know the window frame. CSI 15 t (screen px) silent.
#   D-19T     CSI 19 t (screen size in characters) answers the grid size, like 18 t (there is no display behind a grid): xterm
#             answers root-window pixels / cell pixels. Recommended because a silent 19 t makes `resize -s`-style probes time out.
#   D-TSTACK  Supersedes ADR 0022's D-TSTACK for push/pop only (reports 20/21 t stay silent). Stack depth 10 (xterm
#             MAX_SAVED_TITLES), a push onto a full stack drops the OLDEST entry (xterm overwrites a ring slot; the 10 most
#             recent are kept either way). 22;0 / 22;2 / 22 push the window title; 22;1 (icon) is a no-op because the icon name is not
#             modelled (D-OSC1); 23;0 / 23;2 / 23 pop and emit Request::SetTitle; 23;1 is a no-op; pop on an empty stack does nothing;
#             a third parameter (22;2;N direct slot access) voids the sequence. The stored title is the one the terminal last emitted
#             (post-sanitising); before any OSC 0/2 it is the empty string, so popping it emits SetTitle("") = the frontend default.
#   D-RQM0    DECRQM answers for EVERY query, with 0 for modes Tessera does not know (xterm too): programs that send several queries
#             followed by DA1 (neovim) match replies in order and must not see a missing reply.
#   D-RQSS    DECRQSS: answers m, r, " p, SP q; every other Pt (including " q DECSCA until #95, s DECSLRM until #97, t, $|, *|) answers
#             DCS 0 $ r ST. SGR reply uses xterm's order and its colon forms (38:5:n, 38:2::r:g:b), and reports a curly/dotted/dashed
#             underline as 4:3/4:4/4:5 (xterm only ever prints ;4; kitty prints 4:3 and neovim's probe needs it, [VT] [KT]).
#   D-SECURITY Replies never contain text the program supplied (no title, no icon label, no OSC payload echoed), except the colour
#             echo of 10-colors; CSI 20/21 t, 11/13/15 t, XTGETTCAP (DCS + q), XTGETXRES and DECRQUPSS stay silent.
#   D-ORDER   A reply is queued the moment its query completes, in query order, also inside one chunk; a query cut by a chunk
#             boundary is answered once, when it completes (the Chunking harness checks this).
#
# =============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ DA. Primary, secondary, tertiary device attributes

### DA01_da1_plain
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[c
reply: \e[?64;22c
cite: [CTL] "CSI Ps c Send Device Attributes (Primary DA). Ps = 0 or omitted -> request attributes"; [XT] CASE_DA1 `GetParam(0) <= 0`; D-DA1 (level 4 default, conformance_level() == 4, only implemented features)
flags: decision

### DA02_da1_ps0
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[0c
reply: \e[?64;22c
cite: [CTL] as DA01; explicit Ps = 0
flags: decision

### DA03_da1_nonzero_param_silent
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[1c\e[2c\e[?c\e[?0c
reply: none
cite: [XT] CASE_DA1 answers only when GetParam(0) <= 0; `CSI ? c` is a different (private) sequence xterm does not route to DA1
flags: xterm-quirk negative

### DA04_decid_esc_z
size: 24x80
step: feed \eZ
reply: \e[?64;22c
cite: [XT] CASE_DECID answers the DA1 reply (VT100-compatible identification, DEC STD 070 DECID); D-DECID
flags: decision

flags: decision xterm-quirk

size: 24x80

reply: \e[?0u\e[?64;22c
cite: [KT] keyboard protocol detection: query `CSI ? u` immediately followed by `CSI c`; a terminal that supports the protocol answers `CSI ? flags u` BEFORE the DA1 reply (here flags 0 = nothing pushed); neovim tui.c L309..314 relies on that order; D-ORDER
flags: decision control

flags: control

flags: control

cite: [XT] CASE_DSR handles 5 and 6 only (plus the private ones); 0 and 3 are the terminal's own answers (DEC STD 070), never answered

### DSR06_cpr_pending_wrap_reports_last_column

step: feed \e[1;1Habcdefghij\e[6n
reply: \e[1;10R
cite: [XT] CASE_CPR reports cur_col + 1; xterm keeps the cursor on the last column with the wrap flag set, so the report is column 10, not 11. Vim's t_u7 cursor probe relies on this

### DSR25_dec_locator_below_level3_silent
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[62"p\e[?55n\e[?56n

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ RM. DECRQM / DECRPM (CSI Ps $ p -> CSI Ps ; Pm $ y, CSI ? Ps $ p -> CSI ? Ps ; Pm $ y)
# Pm: 0 not recognised, 1 set, 2 reset, 3 permanently set, 4 permanently reset ([CTL] "CSI Ps $ p"; [DEC] VT510 RM DECRPM).
# xterm does not gate DECRQM on the conformance level (CASE_RQM / CASE_DECRQM), nor does D-RQM0.

### RM03_ansi_srm_permanently_set

### KT07_kitty_query_with_param_silent
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[?1u
note: lead edit 2026-10-31: `\e[?0u` dropped. The parser (vte 0.15) reports `CSI ? 0 u` exactly like the query `CSI ? u`, so Tessera answers it; the echo loop with a raw-echoing peer (the flags-0 reply equals the query) is an accepted risk (ADR 0024)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ RQ. DECRQSS (DCS $ q Pt ST -> DCS 1 $ r Pt' ST, or DCS 0 $ r ST)
# [CTL] "DCS $ q Pt ST Request Status String (DECRQSS), VT420 and up ... xterm responds with DCS 1 $ r Pt ST for valid requests,
# replacing the Pt with the corresponding CSI string, or DCS 0 $ r ST for invalid requests." The reply Pt is the setting in the form of the
# CSI sequence that would set it, WITHOUT the CSI introducer (m, r, SP q, " p keep their intermediates and final).
# The request ends with ST (ESC \ ) or BEL is NOT a DCS terminator; CAN/SUB abort (tessera-vt emits DcsEnd). Replies end with ESC \ .

flags: control

### RQ34_decrqss_aborted_by_can_is_still_answered

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ TS. Title stack (CSI 22 ; Ps t push, CSI 23 ; Ps t pop)
# [CTL] "Ps = 22;0 save icon and window title on stack, 22;1 icon, 22;2 window; 23;0/1/2 restore ... 22 and 23 accept an optional third
# parameter for direct access to the stack. Parameters in the range 1 through 10 may be used to store the title into the stack or retrieve
# the title from the stack without pushing/popping." [XT] xtermPushTitle/xtermPopTitle, MAX_SAVED_TITLES 10. D-TSTACK.
# `set title` below is the title already emitted. A pop emits Request::SetTitle(restored); a push emits nothing and replies nothing.

### TS03_push_pop_without_second_param
size: 24x80
step: set title shell
step: feed \e[22t\e]2;a\e\\\e[23t
reply: none
requests: [SetTitle("a"), SetTitle("shell")]
cite: [XT] zero_if_default(1) -> 0 (both); [CTL] "Ps = 22" alone is the dtterm form
flags: control

### TS04_icon_only_is_noop
size: 24x80
step: set title shell
step: feed \e[22;1t\e]2;x\e\\\e[23;1t
reply: none
requests: [SetTitle("x")]
cite: D-TSTACK: vim's t_Si / t_Ri (`22;1t` / `23;1t`, term.c L538) must not disturb the window title; the icon title is not modelled, so both are no-ops and the pop emits nothing
flags: decision

cite: [XT] xtermPopTitle: `--used` index, last in first out
flags: control

### TS08_push_before_any_title_restores_default
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[22;2t\e]2;x\e\\\e[23;2t
reply: none
requests: [SetTitle("x"), SetTitle("")]
cite: D-TSTACK: the stored title was the empty one (no OSC yet); SetTitle("") = "frontend default" (ADR 0022 D-EMPTY)
flags: decision

### TS09_depth_ten_drops_oldest
size: 24x80
step: set title t0
step: feed \e[22;2t\e]2;t1\e\\\e[22;2t\e]2;t2\e\\\e[22;2t\e]2;t3\e\\\e[22;2t\e]2;t4\e\\\e[22;2t\e]2;t5\e\\\e[22;2t\e]2;t6\e\\\e[22;2t\e]2;t7\e\\\e[22;2t\e]2;t8\e\\\e[22;2t\e]2;t9\e\\\e[22;2t\e]2;t10\e\\\e[22;2t\e]2;t11\e\\
step: feed \e[23;2t\e[23;2t\e[23;2t\e[23;2t\e[23;2t\e[23;2t\e[23;2t\e[23;2t\e[23;2t\e[23;2t\e[23;2t
reply: none
requests: [SetTitle("t1"), SetTitle("t2"), SetTitle("t3"), SetTitle("t4"), SetTitle("t5"), SetTitle("t6"), SetTitle("t7"), SetTitle("t8"), SetTitle("t9"), SetTitle("t10"), SetTitle("t11"), SetTitle("t10"), SetTitle("t9"), SetTitle("t8"), SetTitle("t7"), SetTitle("t6"), SetTitle("t5"), SetTitle("t4"), SetTitle("t3"), SetTitle("t2"), SetTitle("t1")]
cite: D-TSTACK, [XT] MAX_SAVED_TITLES 10. Eleven pushes save the title current at each push (t0, t1, ..., t10); the depth is 10, so t0 is dropped and t1..t10 remain. The OSC sets give the first eleven SetTitle (t1..t11); the eleven pops restore t10, t9, ..., t1 and the eleventh pop finds the stack empty (no request). xterm's ring buffer differs: its `used` counter reaches 11, so the 11th pop returns slot 0 again (the stale t10)
flags: decision xterm-quirk

### TS10_direct_slot_param_voids
size: 24x80
step: set title a
step: feed \e[22;2;1t\e]2;b\e\\\e[23;2;1t\e[23;2t
reply: none
requests: [SetTitle("b")]
cite: D-TSTACK: the third (slot) parameter of [CTL] is not supported; both forms are ignored whole and the plain pop finds an empty stack
flags: decision

### TS11_unknown_second_param_ignored
size: 24x80
step: set title a
step: feed \e[22;3t\e]2;b\e\\\e[23;3t\e[22;9t\e[23;9t
reply: none
requests: [SetTitle("b")]
cite: [XT] xtermPushTitle with an unmatched `which` switch case stores an empty item; Tessera ignores values other than 0, 1, 2 (no push, no pop)
flags: decision

### TS12_title_stack_per_terminal_survives_ris
size: 24x80
step: set title a
step: feed \e[22;2t\ec\e[23;2t
reply: none
requests: [SetTitle("a")]
cite: unverified: xterm keeps `saved_titles` across RIS (ReallyReset does not free it); a program that pushes then a shell `reset`s then pops still gets its title back
flags: decision unverified

### TS13_title_pop_is_not_sanitised_twice_and_not_capped_again
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]2;a\u{202e}b\e\\\e[22;2t\e]2;x\e\\\e[23;2t
reply: none
requests: [SetTitle("ab"), SetTitle("x"), SetTitle("ab")]
cite: ADR 0022 D-TITLE-SAN: the stored title is the sanitised one (U+202E removed once); a pop re-emits exactly what the terminal emitted before
flags: control

### TS14_title_stack_bounded_memory
size: 24x80
step: feed (1,000,000 times) \e[22;2t
reply: none
cite: depth 10 bounds memory; each push stores at most MAX_TITLE_BYTES (1024) -> at most 10 KiB. Generated by the test, not stored literally
flags: security

>abcd |
>
>

cite: title ops are silent on the grid and the reply path

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ RP. Reply path behaviour

### RP01_queries_in_one_chunk_replied_in_order
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[5n\e[6n\e[c\e[>q\e[?25$p
reply: \e[0n\e[1;1R\e[?64;22c\eP>|Tessera <VERSION>\e\\\e[?25;1$y
cite: D-ORDER
flags: control

### RP02_reply_independent_of_surrounding_text
size: 3x10
step: feed ab\e[6ncd\e[6n
screen:
>abcd |
>
>
cursor: (0,4)
reply: \e[1;3R\e[1;5R
cite: each CPR sees the cursor at its own position in the stream
flags: control

### RP03_dsr_first_param_decides
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[1;6n\e[0;6n
reply: none
cite: [XT] CASE_DSR switches on GetParam(0) (1 and 0 are not handled); the second parameter is not consulted.
flags: xterm-quirk negative

### RP04_query_interrupted_by_esc_is_not_answered
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[6\e[c
reply: \e[?64;22c
cite: ESC restarts the sequence; only the `CSI c` completes (tessera-vt)
flags: negative control

### RP05_query_interrupted_by_can_is_not_answered
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[6\x18n\e[5\x1an
reply: none
cite: CAN/SUB abort a CSI; the following `n` is printed text, not a final byte
flags: negative control

### RP06_8bit_c1_csi_introducer_query
size: 24x80
step: feed \u{9b}6n
reply: none
cite: unverified: tessera-vt treats U+009B (UTF-8 C2 9B) as printable (the stream is UTF-8; a raw 0x9B byte is invalid UTF-8). No reply expected. 8-bit introducers are #96's area
flags: unverified negative

### RP07_replies_are_bytes_not_requests_of_other_kinds
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[6n
reply: \e[1;1R
requests: []
cite: a Reply is not a SetTitle/Bell/Resize; `requests:` lists only non-Reply requests and is empty here
flags: control

### RP08_reply_with_bell_between
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[5n\x07\e[5n
reply: \e[0n\e[0n
requests: [Bell]
cite: order of Reply and Bell relative to each other is not asserted (separate lists), only each list's own order
flags: control

### RP09_big_flood_bounded
size: 24x80
step: feed (1,000,000 times) \e[6n
cite: Terminal level: 1,000,000 replies are produced (the terminal does not drop; the BOUND lives in app-core's outbox, brief "Reply routing"); the test only checks the first and last replies and that take_requests() returns them without quadratic behaviour. Generated by the test
flags: security

### RP10_reply_not_produced_by_the_terminals_own_reply_form
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[1;1R\e[?64;22c\e[0n\e[?1;2$y\e[?13n\e[8;24;80t\e[>1;10100;0c\eP>|Tessera 0.1.0\e\\
note: lead edit 2026-10-31: `\e[?0u` dropped. The parser (vte 0.15) reports `CSI ? 0 u` exactly like the query `CSI ? u`, so Tessera answers it; the echo loop with a raw-echoing peer (the flags-0 reply equals the query) is an accepted risk (ADR 0024)
reply: none
cite: reply forms are never queries: `R`, `?...c`, `0n`, `$y`, `8;..t`, `>..c`, `DCS > |`, `?0u` all fall through as inert (no feedback loop with an echoing program). The xterm DECRQM `$p` form differs from the `$y` reply form
flags: negative control
